item.description: Likely to be discussed also are tensions in the South China Sea, for which ASEAN ‌and China are, after nearly 10 years, still trying to conclude a code of ​conduct to prevent disputes from escalating ASEAN's top diplomats meet in shadow of U. S.-Iran conflict.

item.title: Russian attacks kill six in Kyiv, other cities; expose gaps in Ukraine’s air defences
item.description: Moscow has in recent weeks stepped up its use of ballistic missiles as it seeks to choke off Ukrainian strikes on oil facilities deep inside Russia that have caused critical fuel shortages affecting both the military and the civilian population. Russian attacks kill six in Kyiv, other cities; expose gaps in Ukraine’s air defences.

item.title: Central Asian Countries Face Fuel Shortages As Russian Oil Exports Drop Off
item.description: Russia is experiencing severe fuel shortages as a result of Ukrainian strikes on its energy infrastructure, resulting in high prices and long lines for gasoline. Now Central Asian countries, which rely heavily on imports of Russian petroleum products, are seeing similar price hikes and shortages. Central Asian Countries Face Fuel Shortages As Russian Oil Exports Drop Off.

item.title: Iran hits out at Gulf neighbours as U.S. presses on with strikes
item.description: Oil prices surged to a one-month high as the United States and Iran tussled for control of the vital strait, with Brent crude rising above $91 a barrel. the highest price since June 11 Iran hits out at Gulf neighbours as U. item.title: Russian And Ukraine Exchange Overnight Strikes As Drone Attacks Target Moscow Region
item.description: Large plumes of black smoke rose high into the skies of the Moscow region on July 20 after Ukrainian drone strikes hit an oil depot and logistics facilities, wounding 10 people as Kyiv vowed to respond to deadly Russian attacks that have left several people dead. Russian And Ukraine Exchange Overnight Strikes As Drone Attacks Target Moscow Region.

item.title: China’s mega-oiler could break America’s Pacific base edge
item.description: China’s construction of what may be the world’s largest naval replenishment ship signals its growing expeditionary ambitions. and highlights the vulnerability of the US’s base-dependent model of power projection. This month, multiple media outlets reported that satellite imagery and state media indicate that a state-owned subsidiary of China State Shipbuilding Corporation (CSSC) has been [] The China’s mega-oiler could break America’s Pacific base edge.

item.title: From the General Assembly to Harlem: Mandela’s call to action endures
item.description: Sixty-seven minutes. That is how long volunteers spent serving lunch to people experiencing food insecurity at Refettorio Harlem in New York City last week – one for every year Nelson Mandela gave to public service. From the General Assembly to Harlem: Mandela’s call to action endures.

item.title: Haiti endures violence and hunger, but hopes grow for a more secure future
item.description: After years of violence perpetrated by gangs, widespread insecurity and the displacement of almost 1.5 million people as well as growing humanitarian needs, Haitians are glimpsing signs of hope as a path to democratic elections begins to emerge. At UN Headquarters in New York, the 15-member Security Council discusses what next for Haiti. Full live coverage below. Haiti endures violence and hunger, but hopes grow for a more secure future.

item.title: Australia-India partnership deep on security, shallow on trade
item.description: The third India-Australia Annual Summit in Melbourne on July 9 produced outcomes across defense, energy, critical minerals, technology and education. 18 in all. But by far the most significant deliverable centered on Australian uranium exports to India. After nearly 12 years of a civil nuclear agreement on paper, Australia and India finalized the administrative [] The post Australia-India partne. Australia-India partnership deep on security, shallow on trade.

item.title: Outsourcing US deterrence: PIPIR and the Asian allies left exposed
item.description: America’s Asia-Pacific defense decentralization policy is rooted in a systemic crisis gripping its military-industrial complex. The breaking point has come to light amid its ongoing conflict with Iran, combined with a protracted maritime campaign against Houthi militants in the Red Sea. These conflicts have forced the US military to expend long-range precision munitions and air-defense [] The pos Outsourcing US deterrence: PIPIR and the Asian allies left exposed.

item.title: A propagandistic Voice of America hands strategic victory to adversaries
item.description: The war with Iran is driving fuel shortages and inflation around the world, deepening anti-American sentiment at a time when international confidence in the United States is already in decline. A June Pew survey found unfavorable views of the rising across 36 countries. This is precisely the moment Washington needs credible international broadcasting to explain its policies [] The post A propagan.

item.title: Middle East Countries On High Alert As US Continues Strikes On Iran
item.description: Air raid sirens blared in Bahrain and other Gulf states as the struggle for control of the Strait of Hormuz continued after US forces conducted a ninth day of air strikes on targets around Iran. Middle East Countries On High Alert As US Continues Strikes On Iran.

item.title: A former Ferrari boss has a blunt message: Your commute is more dangerous than his old job
item.description: Jean Todt spent decades around the deadliest motorsport on Earth. He was a rally co‑driver, then ran Ferrari’s Formula One team, then became president of world motorsport’s governing body. In his early years, a driver dying at the track barely made news. A former Ferrari boss has a blunt message: Your commute is more dangerous than his old job.

item.title: 'Sooner Or Later This Problem Will Be On Your Soil': Estonia Pushes Europe To Bar Russian Fighters
item.description: As Russia's war against Ukraine reshapes Europe's security landscape, Estonia is closely watching the Kremlin's next moves. In an interview with RFE/RL, Estonia's Undersecretary for Internal Security Joosep Kaasik discusses why Tallinn believes prevention is Europe's best defense. 'Sooner Or Later This Problem Will Be On Your Soil': Estonia Pushes Europe To Bar Russian Fighters.

item.title: 'We Have To Be Realists' Regarding Threats From Russia
item.description: Joosep Kaasik, the undersecretary for internal security in Estonia's Ministry of the Interior, told RFE/RL in an interview that his country takes the threat of a potential Russian attack seriously, but is also prepared to deal with the use of soft power by its Eastern neighbor. 'We Have To Be Realists' Regarding Threats From Russia.

item.title: ‘We are preserving a tradition’: how Ghana’s sensationalist film posters became collectible art
item.description: Hand-painted works are often wildly unfaithful to the movies they portray – reinterpretations that sometimes resulted in threats, insults and even physical attacks from viewers who felt dupedSitting on his porch in Teshie near Accra, Heavy J dipped a brush into red oil paint and dabbed it carefully on to his canvas – a flour sack – adding blood to a knife being wielded by a man.

item.title: New US Attacks On Roads, Bridges Reported As Iran Hits Back At Gulf States
item.description: US strikes on Iran widened early on July 18 from the Strait of Hormuz hotspot to multiple sites throughout central and southern Iran, including through the use of fighter jets, while Iran continued to pound US Gulf allies, as a fragile cease-fire further tattered. New US Attacks On Roads, Bridges Reported As Iran Hits Back At Gulf States.

item.title: Australia updates travel advice for Laos as charges announced over mass methanol poisoning
item.description: Distillery owner could face only three months in jail over alleged poisoning of Australian teenagersGet our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcastThe Australian government has increased its travel alert level for Laos, advising travellers to “exercise a high degree of caution” due to the risk of methanol poisoning. Australia updates travel advice for Laos as charges announced over mass methanol poisoning.
